Travel Camera Insurance Guide

Camera gear is expensive and fragile. One drop, one theft, one ocean wave — and your $3,000 kit is gone. Here's how to protect it.

📋 Types of Coverage

1. Home/Renter's Insurance Rider

Add a "personal articles" rider to your existing policy. Covers theft and damage worldwide. Typically costs $10-20 per $1,000 of coverage annually.

2. Dedicated Camera Insurance

Companies like Hill & Usher and TCP Insurance specialize in camera gear. They cover professional use, rental equipment, and international travel.

3. Travel Insurance with Gear Coverage

World Nomads and SafetyWing offer gear coverage as add-ons. Good for single trips but limits are usually lower ($1,000-2,500).

🛡️ What to Look For

  • Worldwide coverage: Essential for international travel
  • Theft protection: Most common claim type
  • Accidental damage: Drops, water, sand
  • No depreciation: "Replacement cost" vs "actual cash value"
  • Fast claims: You need gear replaced quickly on the road
⚠️ Read the Fine Print: Most policies exclude "mysterious disappearance" (you lost it) and "wear and tear." Some exclude specific countries.
